k: Got better while the days of stoning remain? Shafi'is: no need to repeat, though repeating is recommended (al-Nawawi; al-Shinqiti). Malik: repeat what was thrown for you, and a dam is owed (al-Muwatta). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
Healthy, and only worried about the crowd? Go at a quieter time, such as the night (allowed by most scholars; the Hanbali school: the next day after midday), rather than delegate (Ibn Baz).

If you can, follow the time and say the takbir where you are: Imam Ahmad liked the person to be present if able, and Malik said the sick person says the takbir in his lodging at the time (al-Mughni; al-Muwatta).

Who stones: a trustworthy person who is on Hajj this year (the Standing Committee). They begin with themselves: at each jamrah they throw seven for themselves, then seven for you, then move on. They do not need to finish all three for themselves first (Ibn Baz; Ibn Uthaymin).

Yes, if you cannot do it yourself, or only with real hardship: illness, old age, pregnancy, blindness or weakness, or a mother with small children and no one to mind them. A guardian also stones for a small child. Delegation is permitted by all four schools (al-Mughni); the Malikis add that the one unable still owes a dam (al-Muwatta; Mukhtasar Khalil). The Companions stoned on behalf of the children (Ibn Majah {1}: weak chain, its meaning is accepted).

Every hadith quoted is cited to its collection and was checked against the source text; weak narrations are avoided or marked. It is a study companion, not a fatwa service — ask a scholar for rulings on your situation. Scholar review is pending; corrections are welcome.
Only on your phone. There is no account and no server. Export a backup from Settings before changing phones; the document vault is encrypted with your PIN and cannot be recovered without it.
Yes — no ads, no subscriptions, no "pro" tier. Built as sadaqah jariyah for the Ummah. If it helps you, share it and make dua for those who built it.

Yes. Open it once with internet and it caches itself; the counters, rites guide, duas, places and your data all work offline. Prayer times work offline too (the Umm al-Qura month is cached, and computed times fill any gap); the map links need signal — the Show driver card on every place works offline.

Arrived any time before Fajr on the {1}th? Your <1>wuquf is valid</1> — "whoever comes [to Arafah] on the night of Jam', before Fajr, has caught the Hajj" (Tirmidhi {2}); go on to Muzdalifah with the group. Did not reach Arafah at all before Fajr? The Hajj is missed for this year: you exit ihram by the acts of Umrah (tawaf, sa'i, cutting the hair), a hady is owed according to the majority (Hanafis: none), and the Hajj is repeated another year — the obligation still stands. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar before you do anything.

Islam planned for you. <1>Muzdalifah:</1> leave after midnight with your carer — the Prophet ﷺ sent the weak of his family ahead (Bukhari {1}); nothing is owed. The time of the stoning then differs: Shafi'is and Hanbalis allow it from after midnight (Asma stoned before Fajr, Bukhari {2}); Hanafis and Malikis hold it is valid only from Fajr — follow your group's school, and if unsure wait for Fajr, which is valid for everyone. <2>Stoning:</2> appoint someone who has stoned for themselves to throw on your behalf (permitted by all four schools — Ibn Majah {3} has a weak chain, its meaning is accepted; Malikis add a dam for the one unable) — your group leader can arrange it; or go at night (allowed by most scholars), when the bridge is quieter. <3>Tawaf and sa'i:</3> wheelchairs are valid — the Prophet ﷺ performed tawaf mounted (Bukhari {4}); wheelchairs (free or rented at official points around the Haram) and electric carts (upper floors and roof) are available — ask the Haram staff. Illness is not a shortcoming in your Hajj. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

Mina is a grid of numbered camps: find your <1>maktab / camp number</1> on your wristband or card and show it to any scout (kashaf), security officer or the guides for lost pilgrims at the street corners — they will walk you there. No wristband? Say your country and group name; the Hajj mission tents of each country are signposted. Phones struggle in Mina: agree a meeting time and place with your family every morning. Emergency: <2>{1}</2>; Ministry of Hajj care line <3>{2}</3>. Never leave Mina to look for your group in Makkah. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

Shaved before the sacrifice, stoned after shaving, tawaf before stoning — the Prophet ﷺ was asked about every one of these on the Day of Nahr and answered <1>"do it, there is no harm"</1> (Bukhari {1}, {2}; Muslim {3}). Just complete what is left. Shafi'is and Hanbalis say nothing is owed; Hanafis: a dam for shaving before the stoning, or (Qiran / Tamattu') for sacrificing before the stoning or shaving before the hady; Malikis: a fidyah for shaving before the stoning, and a dam for a tawaf al-ifadah done before it. Tell your group leader so the rest of the day is sequenced right, and ask a scholar if your group follows the Hanafi school.

Still near Makkah (Shafi'is and Hanbalis: under about {1} km, the distance for shortening prayers; Hanafis: before passing the miqat)? <1>Go back and do it</1> — nothing is owed. Already far or home? The majority say a dam is owed (a sheep in the Haram — arranged through someone trustworthy there); Malikis consider the farewell tawaf a sunnah with nothing owed. Sisters who left while menstruating owe nothing at all (Bukhari {2}). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

Stop the act, remove the cause, put the ihram back on and continue — the Hajj stands. <1>Forgetting or not knowing:</1> Shafi'is and Hanbalis excuse perfume and clothing but not cutting hair or nails; Hanafis and Malikis require the fidyah regardless; some Hanbalis and many contemporary scholars say nothing is owed (Bukhari {1} — a man in a perfumed cloak was simply told to remove it). A <2>deliberate</2> violation (perfume, cutting hair or nails, men covering the head or wearing stitched clothes) needs the fidyah by all once it reaches each school's threshold: fast three days, or feed six poor people, or slaughter a sheep (Quran {2}; the amounts are from the hadith of Ka'b ibn Ujrah, Bukhari {3}) — Hanafis give this choice only when there was an excuse; without one they require a sheep. Below the threshold less is owed — for hair, a mudd of food per hair under three hairs (Shafi'is and Hanbalis) or a charity under a quarter of the head (Hanafis). <3>Intimacy</3> is different: before the first tahallul (Hanafis: before Arafah) it spoils the Hajj — you still complete it and repeat it another year, and a camel (badanah) is owed (Malikis: a hady; Hanafis: a sheep). After Arafah but before shaving, Hanafis say the Hajj stands and a camel is owed (after shaving, a sheep). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar whether a fidyah applies to you.

The Quran gives the alternative itself: <1>fast three days during Hajj and seven when you return home — ten in all</1> (Quran {1}). Best the {2}th–{3}th (Shafi'i) or the {4}th–{5}th (Hanafi / Hanbali — the {6}th is allowed for the one who owes this fast; a pilgrim with nothing to make up does not fast Arafah). Missed them? Malikis and Hanbalis allow the days of tashriq (Bukhari {7}–{8}), as does al-Shafi'i's old view; the relied-upon Shafi'i view does not, so the three days are made up later; Hanafis say the hady is then owed instead. Many groups can also sponsor a voucher — ask. Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.

You have not lost the Hajj. <1>Stone it the next day, in order:</1> yesterday's jamarat first (small→middle→Aqabah; only Aqabah if you missed the {1}th), then today's — all after midday. The stoning is made up: Shafi'is and Hanbalis say nothing more is owed; Hanafis and Malikis say a <2>dam</2> (a sheep, slaughtered and given to the poor of the Haram) is owed for the delay. If the {2}th passes with any stoning undone, a dam is owed by all. If you cannot physically go, <3>delegate</3> it to someone who has already stoned for themselves (permitted by all four schools — Ibn Majah {3} has a weak chain, its meaning is accepted; Malikis add a dam for the one unable). Tell your group leader / ask a scholar.
